title: Chat should show refined text, not raw — and label what it pertains to

chat.text: Owner's ask, voice session /framework/ (2026-10-04 ~21:02): 1) The chat bubble for a dictated line is currently the raw, messy self-correcting transcript — once the AI refines a prompt (and we're already paying ~20¢/prompt for that refine), the chat should show the REFINED version as the main bubble, not the raw one. 2) Clicking through should still reach the raw original, for when you need to see why something came out the way it did — don't lose that, just don't lead with it. 3) Separately, today the "refined" expansion/details content itself is unclear out of context — it doesn't say what it pertains to or what it produced. The owner called this a major priority: whenever context could be missing, make it abundantly clear what a shown piece of text is and what produced it. This is a chat-rendering/content change in ux/Dictate's chat widget (and/or ext chat component per CLAUDE.md law 6 — one chat component, one fix for all surfaces), not a quick one-liner — likely needs a task mastermind once the worktree pool is unblocked.

message.text: Owner expanded this ask (voice, 21:09): the growing text area is the raw transcript, sent to a chat bubble — but today there's no visible refinement structure in the chat itself. Wants: each cleaned sentence gets an id; a structured, drill-down summary of the whole prompt showing every sentence was handled; and a raw → clean → structured toggle, so the owner can trust nothing was dropped or misheard. This is the same underlying ask as the card itself, just with the concrete shape: sentence-level ids + a summary view + a toggle, not just "show refined not raw."
